title: Migration safety and telemetry guardrails for private deployments
author: Sofia Martinez
summary: This document defines the safety checks, telemetry signals, and automated rollback criteria to use when performing model, runtime, or configuration migrations for Redwood private (VPC/on-prem) deployments. It combines technical thresholds, operator procedures, and templates for quick execution during upgrades and rollbacks.
body:
Overview
=======

Purpose
-------
This page describes the minimal set of operational guardrails and an actionable runbook to reduce customer impact during migrations (model swaps, runtime upgrades, quantization changes, and config tuning) in private deployments. The procedures emphasize observable safety gates, fast decision points, and reproducible rollback actions so operator teams can execute with confidence.

Scope
-----
- Applies to all private deployments (VPC and on-prem) running Redwood runtime >= v4.1 and control-plane integrations.
- Covers: model hot-swap, runtime patching, quantization profile changes, batching/throughput tuning, and critical config flips (auth, egress, KMS rekey).
- Excludes: physical hardware replacement and site-level network reconfiguration (see separate field-installation runbooks).

Prerequisites and preflight checklist
------------------------------------
Before any migration, verify the following:
- Customer acceptance of scheduled maintenance window and rollback SLA.
- Backup: snapshot of runtime state (KV cache, model artifact manifest), config export, and database checkpoint.
- Test harness: reproducible synthetic workload (load generator) and validation prompt set with known golden outputs.
- Telemetry baseline: last 72 hours of metrics (latency P50/P95, token-rate, GPU utilization, error-rate) collected and archived.
- Operator readiness: on-call roster, incident channel, and escalation contacts for the customer.

Roles and responsibilities
--------------------------
- Release owner: coordinates rollout, signs off on canary, and authorizes full switch. Usually Product or Release Engineering.
- Operator: executes steps, monitors telemetry, and runs rollback commands.
- SRE on-call: adjudicates incidents and applies cross-cluster mitigation (traffic steering).
- Customer contact: receives updates, approves extended maintenance beyond agreed window.

Telemetry signals and thresholds (safety gates)
-----------------------------------------------
We rely on both leading (early) signals and lagging (impact) signals. Each migration must declare a set of primary signals and thresholds. The table below is the default safety gate; teams may tighten thresholds per customer SLA. Operators must configure alerts for these signals before starting.

| Signal | Metric source | Canary threshold | Stop & Investigate threshold | Rollback threshold | Rationale |
|---|---|---:|---:|---:|---|
| Request error rate | per-tenant ingress (5m rolling) | <= 0.5% | > 1% | > 2% sustained 5m | Errors indicate compatibility/runtime faults |
| Generation latency P95 | runtime metrics (5m) | <= baseline + 25% | > baseline + 50% | > baseline + 80% sustained 5m | Latency regressions degrade UX |
| Token drop / truncation events | runtime trace logs | 0 | > 0 in canary | >= 3 per minute | Signs of kv-cache or model mismatch |
| GPU memory OOMs | node exporter / runtime | 0 | any OOM | any OOM with degraded throughput | Critical resource failure |
| Model-quality regressions | eval harness (golden prompts) | automated pass | < 95% of golden score | < 90% | Prevent silent quality loss |

Note: "baseline" refers to the 72 hour pre-migration median for the tenant.

Migration runbook (step-by-step)
--------------------------------
1) Preflight (T-60 to T-10 minutes)
   - Confirm snapshots and config exports have completed.
   - Start synthetic load generator aimed at the canary subset (10-25% of tenant traffic).
   - Start continuous golden eval runner against canary model variant.
   - Ensure alerts (above) are active and routed to the migration channel.

2) Canary rollout (T0)
   - Route 10% of traffic to the canary model/runtime using traffic-steering policy.
   - Observe signals for 5–15 minutes. Record a telemetry snapshot at start and end.
   - Run a focused functional smoke test: core prompt set must match golden outputs within tolerance.
   - If any Stop & Investigate threshold is hit: pause rollout, capture logs, and escalate to SRE.

3) Progressive ramp (T+15 to T+90 minutes)
   - If canary is healthy, increment traffic in steps: 25% -> 50% -> 75% -> 100%. Wait 10–20m between steps, validating signals at each step.
   - Maintain synthetic load during ramp to stress throughput and batching behavior.

4) Cutover and verification (T+90+)
   - When at 100%, run full acceptance suite and notify the customer.
   - Archive migration artifacts: telemetry snapshots, config diffs, and logs.

Rollback decision tree and actions
----------------------------------
- Immediate rollback criteria (operator should execute rollback without further approval):
  - Any GPU OOM on production nodes tied to the migration.
  - Error rate exceeds rollback threshold for more than 5 minutes.
  - Automated model-quality score falls below rollback threshold.
- Investigate-and-hold criteria (requires Release owner + SRE signoff):
  - Latency P95 exceed stop threshold but below rollback threshold.
  - Sporadic token truncation events not reproducible on synthetic load.

Rollback procedure (fast path)
1) Execute the predefined rollback play (atomic switch):
   - CLI: redwoodctl deploy rollback --tenant <TENANT> --manifest <PREVIOUS_MANIFEST_ID> --force
   - Verify that traffic steering is reverted: redwoodctl traffic set --tenant <TENANT> --route default
   - Monitor telemetry for recovery of latency and error-rate (expect return to baseline within 10m).
2) If fast-path rollback fails or leaves degraded state:
   - Quarantine the affected tenant: apply rate-limit of 50% and divert non-critical traffic to fallback model variant.
   - Open an incident with SRE + Release owner and capture forensic snapshots.

Automations and runbook helpers
-------------------------------
- Canary automation job template (example JSON payload):
  {
    "canary_percent": 10,
    "watch_period_minutes": 15,
    "signals": ["error_rate", "latency_p95", "model_quality"]
  }

- Example monitoring query (pseudo-PromQL) for canary error rate:
  sum(rate(http_requests_total{tenant=\"TENANT\",variant=\"canary\",code!~\"2..\"}[5m])) / sum(rate(http_requests_total{tenant=\"TENANT\",variant=\"canary\"}[5m]))

- Quick rollback CLI alias (add to operator toolkit):
  alias rbr=\"redwoodctl deploy rollback --tenant $1 --manifest $2 --force && sleep 30 && redwoodctl traffic set --tenant $1 --route default\"

Operational acceptance criteria (post-migration)
-----------------------------------------------
- Production telemetry returns to baseline within 10 minutes for key metrics (P95 latency, error rate).
- No unexplained token-drop events for 60 minutes.
- Customer confirms no functional regressions for a 2-hour validation window or a signed exception is recorded.

Communications templates
-----------------------
- Short incident template for customer:
  \"We detected an issue during the recent model/runtime update affecting <area>. We have initiated a rollback and expect full recovery within <estimate>. We will send a follow-up with root cause and mitigations.\"

- Internal migration start message (to ops channel):
  \"Starting migration for <TENANT> (release <TAG>). Canary 10% for 15m. Alerts configured: error_rate, latency_p95, model_quality. Contacts: <release_owner>, <sre_oncall>.\"

Postmortem and evidence collection
----------------------------------
- For any Stop & Investigate or Rollback event create an incident ticket and collect:
  - Telemetry snapshot (pre/post), logs (runtime + operator actions), config diffs, and model artifact checksums.
  - Attach synthetic workload results and golden eval outputs.
  - Run a comparison analysis and publish a short findings summary within 24 hours.

Appendix: quick-checklist (printable)
-------------------------------------
- [ ] Customer notified and window confirmed
- [ ] Snapshots & config export complete
- [ ] Golden eval harness active
- [ ] Alerts configured and routed
- [ ] Canary JSon job submitted
- [ ] Traffic steering validated
- [ ] Post-migration acceptance verified
